projection.kind: albers conic equal area, one conic per region
projection.formula: n = (sin f1 + sin f2)/2; C = cos^2 f1 + 2 n sin f1; p = sqrt(C - 2 n sin f)/n; p0 = sqrt(C - 2 n sin f0)/n; t = n (l - l0), l - l0 wrapped into -180..180 degrees; x = p sin t; y = p0 - p cos t; screen = [translate[0] + scale*x, translate[1] - scale*y]. f1/f2 = parallels, f0 = origin, l0 = meridian, all in degrees, radians inside. The lower48 region takes every STATEFP that no other region lists. A region with a clip [x0, y0, x1, y1] (screen pixels) draws only inside it, as d3's clipExtent: a point outside it is not drawn and a ring is cut to it.

frame.from: build_district_geo.REGIONS + build_states(cb_2024_us_state_20m.zip); identical to geo/cd119.json projection.regions

forms.albers: JSON; features keyed by id; SVG path strings in the 975x610 frame, "M x y L ... Z" per ring (today's grammar); an anchor inside each
forms.wgs84: GeoJSON FeatureCollection (RFC 7946 winding); properties.id is the GEOID (use promoteId "id"); NAD83 coordinates written as WGS84 (under 2 m apart, far below the 1:500,000 generalisation)

detail.use: zoomed SVG views up to the 40x ceiling

z10.use: MapLibre zooms 10 and up, per state

compat.keys: states by postal code, districts by "<ST>-<NN>"/"<ST>-AL" exactly as geo/cd*.json

hex.size: distance between the centres of neighbouring hexagons (flat-to-flat width)
hex.formula: s = size*1609.344/sqrt(3); qf = (sqrt(3)/3*x - y/3)/s; rf = (2/3*y)/s; cube-round with floor(v+0.5); x, y = EPSG:5070 metres from NAD83 longitude/latitude
hex.membership: every hexagon touching a 500k state outline; home state = the outline holding its centre, else the largest overlap

zcta_home.basis: the state whose 500k outline holds the ZCTA gazetteer internal point, else the nearest outline within 20 km

steps.step: zcta: homes + one-pass split into per-state parquet
zcta: homes + one-pass split into per-state parquet
zcta: homes + one-pass split into per-state parquet

notes: Hawaii is clipped to its extent (build_district_geo REGIONS['hawaii']['clip'], the canvas around the Hawaii box one pixel clear of the Alaska, lower-48 and American Samoa boxes), as d3's geoAlbersUsa clips each inset to its clipExtent (2026-09-26): the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands, which the 500k files carry and the 20m fit never held, are removed and counted (clipped_rings; a feature left with nothing is listed under clipped), and no Hawaiian pixel moves. Rings wholly off the canvas are still dropped and counted (offcanvas_rings); after the clip there are none.

The Alaska conic wraps longitude into [-180, 180] degrees like d3's geoAlbersUsa (2026-09-26): the Near Islands east of 180 degrees draw at the west end of the Aleutian chain, and the inset takes the 0.35 x lower-48 cap (scale 376.54) instead of the 254.24 the unwrapped vertices forced on the fit.

A national layer that is not one valid coverage is simplified region by region (simplify_regions), never per feature for the whole nation: before the Hawaii clip, French Frigate Shoals, drawn by the Hawaii conic inside the Alaska box, overlapped the Kenai Peninsula at Alaska's corrected scale.

American Samoa, Guam and the Northern Marianas have no placement in the frame (the 20m state file has no polygon for them): they are in every wgs84 file and in the lookup tables, and counted as unplaced in the albers ones.

Congressional districts come from the 20m files only (no 500k district file is cached): albers/national, wgs84/z0 and wgs84/z5, never wgs84/z10, where 1:20,000,000 lines would sit a kilometre or more off the 500k tracts.
A ZCTA belongs to the state holding its gazetteer internal point (else the nearest outline within 20 km); a ZCTA crossing a state line is drawn whole in that state's file only.
Two levels that follow the same boundary (a county edge and its tracts' edges) are simplified separately and can differ by up to the tier tolerance.
